title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a law enforcement deployment. A system built to support policing work was queried by an officer for a personal purpose, and the checks that should separate legitimate queries from personal ones did not stop him. The reported searches ran across the Flock camera system and other law enforcement databases over two years, which means the misuse was repeated rather than a single slip.

Catching this would have required query auditing that flags searches tied to an officer's own contacts, and a review process that acts on those flags. The woman's own discovery of the searches, after she had changed her identity, phone number and social media habits, indicates the detection came from outside the systems rather than from them.

What is established is an accusation, a criminal complaint filed by the department, an internal affairs investigation, and administrative leave. It is not established that Rogers is guilty of any violation, and the outcome of the Select Board hearing is not yet known.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the abusive relationship about five years ago and changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location using the Flock camera system and other law enforcement databases, including CJIS and CORI, multiple times in 2024 and 2025. She also said he drove by her home and has obtained a restraining order against him.

The Stow Police Department filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 for possible state law violations. After a four-week internal affairs investigation, the department placed him on paid administrative leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. A Select Board hearing is scheduled next week, when town leaders could vote on his employment status. Boston 25 News reached out to Rogers' attorney but has not received a response.
